title: Build reproducible pipeline to generate sanitized public benchmark tables (no sensitive fields)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
## Context
Marketing/Docs need a public-facing data table (CSV + JSON) backing the benchmark report charts (latency/$ and supporting metrics) by model + region + workload. We already have internal raw exports and benchmark-lab output, but we need a *sanitized*, *deterministic*, *versioned* build pipeline with explicit approvals.

This ticket covers the end-to-end pipeline:
- ingestion of benchmark-lab artifacts (or canonical internal table)
- sanitization/redaction of sensitive fields
- deterministic table generation + checksums
- publishing to a stable, cacheable public endpoint used by web/docs
- approvals + sign-off checklist before each refresh

## Goals
- Public tables are safe to publish (no internal infra details, no identifiers, no timestamps that reveal capacity windows)
- Build is reproducible from pinned inputs (commit SHA + artifact hashes)
- Versioning is explicit (benchmark_version) so report claims map to a single dataset
- Easy for Marketing/Docs to consume (simple schema, minimal breaking changes)

## Non-goals
- Publishing raw per-run logs, per-request traces, request IDs, or internal cost breakdowns
- Auto-refreshing continuously (initially manual-triggered per report cadence)

## Proposed public schema (v1)
One row per (benchmark_version, model_id, region, workload).

Required columns:
- benchmark_version (e.g., "2025-02")
- model_id (public-facing catalog slug, e.g., "llama-3.1-70b-instruct")
- model_family (e.g., "Llama", "Qwen")
- region (e.g., "us-east", "eu-west", "ap-southeast")
- workload ("chat" | "embeddings")
- concurrency (integer as string in CSV; keep as numeric-looking string)
- input_tokens_p50 (int)
- output_tokens_p50 (int; for chat)
- latency_ms_p50
- latency_ms_p95
- throughput_tok_s (tokens/sec aggregate at target concurrency)
- cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens (chat) OR cost_usd_per_1m_tokens (embeddings)
- latency_per_dollar (definition per methodology)
- runs_aggregated (count)
- variance_pct_p95 (single number: max(run_to_run_p95_variance_pct); used for “don’t overclaim” guardrail)

Notes:
- Keep naming consistent with benchmark report copy + chart spec.
- Avoid fields that leak infra topology (instance types, GPU model, fleet name), operational windows, or internal routing details.

## Sensitive fields to exclude (explicit deny-list)
Hard exclude if present anywhere upstream:
- request_id / trace_id / span_id
- customer_id / org_id / api_key_id
- hostnames, node IDs, cluster names, GPU UUIDs
- exact run timestamps (ok to keep benchmark_version only)
- internal region codes that don’t match public region names
- per-component cost breakdowns (GPU-hour, egress, control plane)
- error payloads / stack traces

## Build/publish approach
1) Canonical input: benchmark-lab exported artifacts from pinned commit (preferred) OR signed internal raw table snapshot with hash.
2) Sanitizer + schema normalizer:
   - enforce allow-list columns
   - enforce region/model mapping to public slugs
   - compute derived metrics only from already-aggregated values (avoid reintroducing raw data)
3) Deterministic build:
   - commit SHA pinned
   - input artifact hash captured
   - output includes:
     - public_tables_v1.csv
     - public_tables_v1.json
     - manifest.txt (benchmark_version, generator version, input hashes, output hashes)
4) Publish:
   - upload to public bucket/CDN path: /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/{benchmark_version}/tables/
   - update “latest” pointer only after approvals

## Approval checklist (required to flip latest)
- Perf/Evals sign-off (Claire Dubois or Jonas Weber): methodology alignment + sanity checks
- Legal/claims review (Michael Grant): disclaimers/claims guidelines satisfied
- SRE sign-off (Neha Kapoor or Sean Gallagher): publishing doesn’t create operational risk; no internal routing details
- Docs owner ack (Elliot Price): schema stable enough for landing page integration

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pipeline produces CSV + JSON with schema v1 and no denied fields
- [ ] Build is deterministic (re-running with same inputs yields identical hashes)
- [ ] Manifest includes generator version + input/output hashes
- [ ] “Latest” update is gated on explicit approvals (recorded in ticket comment + checkbox)
- [ ] Docs site can fetch table from stable URL without auth
- [ ] Rollback path documented (re-point latest to previous version)

## Implementation tasks
- [ ] Define allow-list + deny-list in code, add unit tests with "poison" fixtures
- [ ] Add schema validation step (fail CI if unexpected columns)
- [ ] Add region/model slug mapping file (reviewed by Marketing + Docs)
- [ ] Add build target to benchmark-lab or standalone generator repo (TBD)
- [ ] Create publish job with dry-run mode and explicit "promote latest" step
- [ ] Document runbook: how to cut a new benchmark_version

## Open questions
- Do we want to publish variance_pct_p95 publicly or keep it internal and only use in copy/FAQ? (Default: publish; it helps credibility, but might invite misinterpretation.)
- Should embeddings cost be expressed per 1M *input* tokens, or total tokens? (Match methodology doc + chart spec.)

## References
- benchmark-lab: PR-159 export csv/json + public table generator (implementation baseline)
- Public claims guidelines: Architecture/Standards > performance-standards > public-benchmarking-claims-guidelines
- Report chart spec + landing page wirecopy (Drive)

Question: are we ok publishing region names as used in docs (us-east/eu-west/ap-southeast) vs cloud provider names? I prefer our docs-friendly labels only.

2025-01-24 (Claire Dubois): Please include runs_aggregated and some variance indicator. We’ve been careful not to overclaim; having a variance number in the public table helps substantiate any “typical range” language in the report. Also: do NOT publish exact run timestamps; benchmark_version is fine.

2025-01-27 (Elliot Price): From docs side, we need stable URLs and a “latest” pointer so we don’t have to change links in the landing page every refresh. Also please keep column names consistent with chart spec (we’re generating some charts in the blog from the JSON).

2025-02-03 (Mei Lin): Update: implemented schema v1 allow-list, deny-list, and a “poison fixture” test (fails build if request_id/trace_id/hostname-like fields appear). Added manifest.txt with input artifact SHA256 + generator git SHA + output hashes. Next: publishing job + approvals gate.

2025-02-06 (Michael Grant): Legal/claims: please ensure naming doesn’t imply endorsement of any third-party provider and that the dataset doesn’t include any customer-identifiable info (sounds covered). 2025-02-10 (Mei Lin): Current status: pipeline works in dry-run. Remaining work: wire publish to public bucket path and implement “promote latest” requiring manual approvals. Also need final decision on embeddings cost naming (per 1M tokens vs input tokens) to match methodology.
